To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tsunami of December 2004 caused severe damage to the island ecosystems of the Andaman and Nicobars, with the islands of the Nicobar group more affected than the Andamans.

(1) The Nicobar Islands suffered more impact compared to the Andamans; (2) the impact of tsunami is visible in the coastal elements like vegetation, plantations, coral reefs, mangroves, beaches and coastal water bodies; (3) the damage is severe in the Andaman islands; (4) the impact of the tsunami in the Nicobar Islands is not severe as in the Andamans and (5) there were no records for some small islands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of tsunami in tropical island ecosystems.
the analysis of the impact of tsunami on the island ecosystems using geospatial techniques.
the assessment of the impact of tsunami and its recovery status in the Andaman and Nicobars using remote sensing techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the islands were affected by the 2004 tsunami and the impact was more on the Nicobar islands than the Andaman islands.
the tsunami had a significant impact on the tropical island ecosystems of Andaman and Nicobars.
the tsunami of December 2004 has left an imprint on the landscape of the islands and the recovery of the ecosystem will take several years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of remote sensing techniques and its integration with GIS is a useful tool for monitoring the changes in coastal ecosystems and to assess the extent of damage caused by natural disasters.
the tsunami had a severe impact on the island ecosystems, and that the impact is still continuing in the form of slow recovery.
this study is a good example for the use of geospatial tools in the field of disaster management and environmental impact assessment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the geospatial technology can be used to analyze the impact of natural disasters and the same can be used to monitor the recovery of the affected ecosystems.
the geospatial technology has a great scope in the study of tsunami and other disasters in tropical island ecosystems.
the tsunami of 2005 has had a profound impact on the tropical islands of Andaman and Nicobars.
